question.title: Higher Rank in the Chart
question.content:
A company chart is stored as a binary tree with unique values. You are given its root and two different nodes a and b that are both in the tree. A node outranks another when it is closer to the root.

Return whichever of the two nodes outranks the other, or null if they are at the same depth.

 

Example 1:

Input: root = [7,3,9,null,4], a = 4, b = 9
Output: 9
Explanation: Node 9 is at depth 1 and node 4 is at depth 2.

Example 2:

Input: root = [7,3,9,null,4], a = 3, b = 4
Output: 3

Example 3:

Input: root = [1,2,3], a = 2, b = 3
Output: null
Explanation: Both nodes are at depth 1.

 

Constraints:

  • The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [2, 104].
  • -105 <= Node.val <= 105
  • All Node.val are unique.
  • a != b
  • a and b will exist in the tree.
